newsitem.title: GERMANY: Quit clucking about reshuffles, Bonn FDP tells CSU.
newsitem.headline: Quit clucking about reshuffles, Bonn FDP tells CSU.

text.p: Germany's liberal Free Democrats (FDP) told another party in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition on Sunday to stop "clucking on" about a possible cabinet reshuffle.
FDP general secretary Guido Westerwelle said Bavaria's Christian Social Union (CSU) should speak to Kohl directly instead of calling for cabinet changes via the media.

"The lack of discipline within the CSU is damaging the image of the coalition," Westerwelle told the Welt am Sonntag weekly newspaper. "All this clucking on about personnel matters from the CSU is only useful the opposition."
Finance Minister Theo Waigel, the CSU leader, has called in several recent interviews for a reshuffle ahead of next year's general election to give the centre-right government new impetus.
He has been backed by Bavarian Premier Edmund Stoiber, another top CSU figure, who has advised Kohl to act like a soccer coach, freshening up his team before an important match.

Kohl, who is holidaying in Austria, told ZDF television on Thursday he saw no need for a reshuffle at the moment but did not rule out the prospect at some point before the election, due in September 1998.
Westerwelle said changes affecting the three FDP members of the cabinet were not on the agenda.
